DAG for the effect of ambient temperature on the timing of birth. (a) Unadjusted model. (b) Adjusted model. IVF: in vitro fertilization; tobacco & others: tobacco, alcohol, and drug use; maternal age: maternal age at birth; comorbidities: pre-pregnancy maternal diseases such as hypertension and diabetes; complications: any medical condition during pregnancy related to mother or fetus such as pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, intrauterine growth restriction, infections, etc. We condition on multiple pregnancy, as we only include singleton births. Produced and analysed by using DAGitty.net.
Characteristics of the study population ( n =
 131 599), Southern Israel, 2005–19.
Conditional associations of mean ambient temperature exposures at specific (selected) gestation weeks with preterm birth. Cox proportional-hazards model with time-dependent covariates integrated with DLNMs, adjusted for seasonality (as a weekly time-varying covariate), ethnicity, and SES. Natural cubic splines with three degrees of freedom were used for exposure–response and lag–response relationships. The numbers above each panel show the week of gestation. The 95% CIs are shown as shaded areas. Reference: minimum-risk temperature (16°C). n =
 131 599; preterm birth events = 9186.
Average estimated absolute and relative risk of preterm birth by temperature exposure trajectories across LMP months. Left side: Top: estimated risk across months of conception and the 95% CIs, as calculated by bootstrapping (500 samples with replacement). Middle: estimated relative risks and the 95% CIs calculated from the same bootstrapping results, with the month of minimal estimated risk (March) defined as the reference. Bottom: distribution of average exposure during Weeks 33–37 of pregnancy by LMP month. Right side: radar plots emphasizing the seasonal pattern of the results; the top and middle plots present the estimates from the model and the bottom plot presents the mean temperatures for the distributions on the left. The exposure in the bottom part of the figure is calculated based on LMP and residential address, regardless of the actual gestational age at birth. Estimations are based on a Cox proportional-hazards model with time-dependent covariates integrated with DLNMs, adjusted for seasonality (as a weekly time-varying covariate), ethnicity, and SES. n =
